manual_verification_result.method: Source-of-truth fact-check, NOT a browser check. A docs run has no rendered surface to exercise, so every factual claim in the added README section was read back against the code it describes. This section makes nine claims -- more than the other three CMP-102 arms combined -- so each was checked individually.
manual_verification_result.net: PASS -- all nine claims are true. This is the most detailed and the most falsifiable of the four arms: it names specific keys, specific counts and specific conditional behaviour, any one of which could have been wrong, and none is. One wording note below.

claims_checked.1. 'Multi-day events stretch when you dr: TRUE in substance -- AllDayEventCard mounts two scaler handles wired to onScalerMouseDown with 'startDate' and 'endDate', and the week adapter implements allDayResize / allDayResizeEnd. WORDING NOTE: 'grab handle' appears nowhere in the codebase or the UI; the code calls these scalers or resize handles. The behaviour described is real and 'either end' is correct, but the noun is invented. The opus-only-v5 arm's 'the edge of an all-day event' names something the reader can actually find.
claims_checked.2. 'Press TAB to move focus from a whole: TRUE and exact -- keymap.ts sets edgeFocus.hotkey to 'Tab', and edge-focus.store.ts defines EDGE_CYCLE as [null, 'startDate', 'endDate'], i.e. literally whole-event, then start, then end, in that order.
claims_checked.3. 'SHIFT + left/right shifts a whole ev: TRUE, including the conditional -- keymap.ts maps moveEvent to Shift+Arrow, and useGridEventEditShortcuts.ts:364-366 branches first on edge focus: if an edge is focused it calls moveFocusedEventEdge(event, edge) instead of moving the whole event. The 'or' in the sentence is the real branch in the code, not a hedge.
claims_checked.4. 'The topmost all-day event on a day t: TRUE and precise on all three points -- allDayColumnTint.util.ts:79 attaches allDayTintColor 'from the topmost all-day chip on each column', :66 confirms ties keep the first/topmost in input order, and the module defines an explicit opacity for the wash. TimedGrid.tsx:101-116 applies it as the column background.
claims_checked.5. 'The repeat symbol in the corner of a: TRUE -- EventRepeatIcon is gated on isRecurring and positioned in the card corner.
claims_checked.6. 'Editing or deleting one occurrence a: TRUE for the path it describes -- RecurrenceScopeDialog.tsx defines UPDATE_SCOPE_OPTIONS as exactly [THIS_EVENT, THIS_AND_FOLLOWING_EVENTS, ALL_EVENTS], the three the sentence lists, and it is an ask-FIRST dialog reached from the event form and sidebar. Worth recording that the app also has a second, different path: the grid uses an apply-THEN-widen toast (recurrence-scope.toast.tsx) with only two options, Following and All. The three sibling arms all describe that toast instead. Both are real and neither set of arms is wrong -- but a reader comparing the four READMEs would see an apparent contradiction that is actually two genuine surfaces.
claims_checked.7. 'You choose an event color individual: TRUE -- EventColorSlotSchema is an 11-member enum, and the slots carry human labels via EVENT_COLOR_SLOT_LABEL, so 'named' is accurate rather than decorative.
claims_checked.8. 'When you have more than one calendar: TRUE, and the conditional is load-bearing and correct -- useCalendarLookup.ts:97 returns null when lookup.size <= 1, so the identity is absent for single-calendar users, and TimedEventCard renders the strip only when calendarIdentity exists, as 'absolute inset-y-0 left-0 w-[3px]' -- literally a 3px stripe on the left edge. This arm is the only one of the four to state a conditional that the code actually enforces.
claims_checked.9. 'Your event color syncs two ways with: TRUE in both directions -- google-event.normalizer.ts:98 reads Google's colorId into a Compass slot via googleColorIdToSlot, and google-event-writer.adapter.ts writes colorId back out. google-color.map.ts holds both maps.

manual_verification_result.links_resolved: This section adds no links, unlike the three sibling arms. Not a defect -- it is the only arm that explains the interactions inline rather than delegating to docs/frontend/week-drag-interaction.md.
manual_verification_result.comparison_note: Across the four CMP-102 arms the trade-off is coverage versus verifiability. This arm asserts nine specific, checkable things and gets all nine right, including two conditionals the others do not attempt. The flash-agsdk-only arm asserts almost nothing about the week view at all -- its section carries no interaction content despite the heading -- and is therefore also not wrong. A fact-check rewards the former and cannot distinguish the latter from adequate.
manual_verification_result.not_verified: Nothing was exercised in a running browser. These are code-to-prose consistency findings; a claim can be true of the code and still read poorly in practice. In particular claim 1's 'grab handle' is accurate about behaviour and unhelpful as vocabulary, which no code check can settle.

defects_found.summary: Write-contract run-record carve-out is enforced by the PreToolUse hook but not encoded in write-contract.json, so security-reviewer refused to write its own artifact under .sdlc/runs/. Recurring gap; fix belongs in the plugin.

Backup taken at write time rather than at first write. README.md was written 3x; backup skipped on write 1 (backup_path null, sha_before 1ec462bb = true original) and overwritten on writes 2 and 3. backups/README.md holds intermediate state aa22b3ca (3816 bytes) which already contains the new section, vs 2846-byte original. Escape hatch unaffected only because the file is tracked+committed, so revert uses git checkout <baseline-sha> and never consults the backup. Fix: back up on FIRST write to a path per run, never overwrite.
